{
  "root_cause": "The disclosure menu does not close when focus leaves the menu tree, causing the dropdown to remain visible and cover page content after tabbing out.",
  "repair_strategy": "Add a focusout listener to the menu element that checks if the related target is outside the menu; if so, and the menu has an open controller, close the controller.",
  "edits": [
    {
      "path": "src/_baseMenu.js",
      "sha256": "659255a214409c4048ca6d6312846a5e9c5c368e5c777b8499f437fdb9418447",
      "before": "/**\\n   * Handles focus events throughout the menu for proper menu use.\\n   *\\n   * - Adds a `focus` listener to every menu item so when it gains focus,\\n   *   it will set the item's containing menu's focus state\\n   *   to \\\"self\\\".\\n   *\\n   * @protected\\n   */\\n  _handleFocus() {\\n    this.elements.menuItems.forEach((menuItem, index) => {\\n      menuItem.dom.link.addEventListener(\\\"focus\\\", () => {\\n        this.focusState = \\\"self\\\";\\n        this.currentChild = index;\\n      });\\n    });\\n  }\\n",
      "after": "/**\\n   * Handles focus events throughout the menu for proper menu use.\\n   *\\n   * - Adds a `focus` listener to every menu item so when it gains focus,\\n   *   it will set the item's containing menu's focus state\\n   *   to \\\"self\\\".\\n   *\\n   * @protected\\n   */\\n  _handleFocus() {\\n    this.elements.menuItems.forEach((menuItem, index) => {\\n      menuItem.dom.link.addEventListener(\\\"focus\\\", () => {\\n        this.focusState = \\\"self\\\";\\n        this.currentChild = index;\\n      });\\n    });\\n\\n    // Close the menu when focus leaves the menu tree\\n    this.dom.menu.addEventListener(\\\"focusout\\\", (event) => {\\n      if (!this.dom.menu.contains(event.relatedTarget)) {\\n        if (this.elements.controller && this.elements.controller.isOpen) {\\n          this.elements.controller.close();\\n        }\\n      }\\n    });\\n  }\\n"
    }
  ],
  "expected_accessibility_effect": "When a user tabs out of the navigation dropdown, the dropdown will close, preventing it from obscuring page content.",
  "functional_risks": [
    "Potential unintended closure if focus moves to an element that is not a DOM descendant of the menu but is logically part of the menu (e.g., a portal).",
    "If the menu is used as a trigger for non‑menu popups, those popups may close prematurely.",
    "Edge cases where rapid focus shifts could cause flicker, though the containment check mitigates this."
  ],
  "verification_requirements": [
    "Tabbing from any menu item to an element outside the menu closes the dropdown (aria-expanded false, submenu hidden).",
    "Moving focus within the menu or into a submenu does not close the dropdown.",
    "Keyboard navigation inside the dropdown (arrow keys, Home, End) continues to work when open.",
    "Clicking the Shop button still opens and closes the dropdown as expected.",
    "Mouse hover behavior remains unchanged."
  ]
}
reasoning:
We need to analyze the problem.

The test scenario:

Journey:
Step 0: seek #shop (tab to home? Actually they start focusing body -> tab to #home etc)
But step sequence: They had focus events: from body->#home seq0, #home->#contact seq1, #contact->#shop seq2, #shop->#plants seq3, #plants->#tools seq4, #tools->#search seq5

Thus they navigated via Tab: starting at some point maybe body? Anyway they ended at #search input.

Assertions expected after leaving navigation (#search):
- After pressing Enter on #shop (which opens dropdown), they expect after moving away (by tabbing out) that #shop aria-expanded becomes false and #plants visible false.

Observed failure: At step 2 (the "Tab out of the navigation to search"), after focusing #search, they assert that #shop aria-expanded == false (but observed true) and #plants visible false (observed true?). Wait observed says: For assertion kind attribute name aria-expanded selector #shop value false, observed "true", pass false. So aria-expanded remained true. And second assertion visible #plants value false observed true pass false. Means dropdown still open and plants still visible.

So issue: When navigating away from the dropdown via Tab (leaving the menu), the dropdown does not close automatically. Expected behavior: When focus leaves the menu (i.e., when tabbing out of the menu), the dropdown should close (aria-expanded false) and submenu hidden.

In many accessible disclosure patterns, pressing Tab to move focus out of the dropdown should close it. Usually handled by listening for focusout or blur on the menu or its items, and if focus leaves the menu, close it.

Looking at the code: In BaseMenu, there is _handleFocus method that sets focusState to self when a menu item gets focus. There's also blurChildren method that blurs all items. But there is no automatic closing on focus loss.

We need to add logic: when focus leaves the menu (i.e., focusState changes from self to none? Or when a menu item loses focus and focus is not within menu), we should close the dropdown if it's open.

Specifically for the Shop button (which is a disclosure menu toggle controlling the submenu). The menu is a DisclosureMenu (top-level). It has a controller (the Shop button) that is a DisclosureMenuToggle. The menu's focusState is managed.

When focus moves from a menu item to outside (like the search input), the menu's focusState should become "none"? Let's see: In _handleFocus, each menuItem's link focus event sets focusState = "self" and currentChild = index. So when focus is on a menu item, focusState is self. When focus leaves the menu item (blur), there is no handler to set focusState to none. However, there is a blur method on BaseMenuItem that blurs the link if parent menu's shouldFocus is true. But that's only called programmatically.

Thus we need to add a blur listener to each menu item's link to set focusState to "none" when it loses focus, and then if focusState is none and the menu is open, close it.

Alternatively, we could listen for focusout on the menu element itself, and if relatedTarget is not inside the menu, close.

Simpler: In BaseMenu's _handleFocus, also add a blur listener to each menuItem's link that sets focusState = "none". Then after setting focusState to none, we can check if the menu is open (i.e., if it has a controller and controller.isOpen) and close it.

But we need to differentiate between moving focus within the menu (e.g., from one item to another) vs leaving. If we set focusState to none on blur, then when focusing next item, focusState will be set to self again (via focus listener). That's fine.

Thus we can close the menu when focusState becomes none and the menu is open (i.e., controller.isOpen). However, we need to ensure we don't close when focus is moving to a submenu? Actually submenu items are part of the submenu, not the top-level menu. When focus goes into a submenu item, the top-level menu's focusState may become none? Let's see: The top-level menu's focusState is set to self when any of its menuItems (including the Shop button? Actually the Shop button is not a menuItem? In the markup, the Shop button is inside a <li> as a button, and the <li> is a menuItem? The menuItemSelector is "li". So each <li> is a menuItem. The Shop button is inside the <li> as a link? Actually it's a button inside the li. The menuLinkSelector is "a". So the link inside the li is the <a> elements (Home, Contact). The Shop button is not an <a>, it's a button, so it's not considered a menuLink. Therefore the Shop button is not a menuItem's link; it's inside the menuItem but not selected as menuLink. So the menuItem for Shop contains a button (toggle) and a submenu ul. The menuItem's link is the button? Wait menuLinkSelector is "a". So they only consider <a> as menu links. Thus the Shop button is not a menuLink, thus not focusable via tab? Actually button is focusable by default. But the menu's focus handling only applies to menuItems' links (the <a>). So the Shop button won't get focusState updates via _handleFocus. However, the Shop button is a controller element (the toggle) that has its own focus handling via BaseMenuToggle? Let's see: In BaseMenu.initialize, if isTopLevel and controller exists, they create a BaseMenuToggle and set it as controller. The BaseMenuToggle likely handles its own focus? Not shown in snippet but likely it has focus/blur handlers? Not in provided code. But we can see that the Shop button has tabindex? It's a button, so focusable.

When focus is on the Shop button, the top-level menu's focusState may not be updated. However, when we press Enter on Shop button, it opens the dropdown. Then we press Tab to move focus to the first link inside dropdown (#plants). At that point, focus is on a menuItem link (since #plants is an <a> inside the submenu). The top-level menu's focusState? The focus is on a submenu item, not a top-level menuItem. The top-level menu's focusState may remain whatever it was (maybe self? Actually when focus entered the Shop button, focusState may not have been set. But after opening, maybe they set focusState to self? Not sure.)

When we then tab from #plants to #tools (still inside submenu), focusState may stay self? When we tab from #tools to #search (outside), focus leaves the submenu and also leaves the top-level menu. At that point, we need to close the dropdown.

Thus we need to detect when focus leaves the entire menu system (including submenus) and close any open top-level disclosure.

Approach: Add a listener for focusout on the menu element (or document) that checks if the relatedTarget is outside the menu's container (including submenus). If so, close the menu.

But we must ensure we don't close when moving focus within the menu or submenu.

Simpler: In BaseMenu's _handleFocus, add a blur listener to each menuItem's link that sets focusState = "none". Then after setting to none, if the menu has a controller and controller.isOpen, close it.

But we need to ensure that when focus moves from a top-level menuItem to a submenuItem (which is not a top-level menuItem's link), the blur on the top-level menuItem's link will fire, setting focusState to none, causing closure incorrectly. However, when focus moves from a top-level menuItem link to a submenuItem link, the top-level menuItem's link loses focus (blur) before the submenuItem link gains focus (focus). So the blur handler would fire, setting focusState to none and potentially closing the menu prematurely.

We need to differentiate: we should only close if the blur's relatedTarget is outside the menu (including its submenus). So we need to check event.relatedTarget.

Thus better to add a focusout listener on the menu element itself (or on the container) and check if the new focus target is outside the menu's tree.

Implementation: In BaseMenu's _handleFocus method, after setting up focus listeners on menuItems, also add a focusout listener to this.dom.menu (the menu element) that checks if the event.relatedTarget is not within this.dom.menu (or any of its submenus?). Actually we want to detect when focus leaves the menu and all its submenus. So we can check if the event.relatedTarget is not a descendant of this.dom.menu (including submenus). If so, close the menu (if it has a controller and controller.isOpen). However, we need to ensure we don't close when focus moves from a menu item to its submenu (which is still a descendant). Since submenu is a descendant of the menu element (the menu element includes submenus? The submenu is positioned absolutely but is still a child of the li? Actually the submenu ul is a child of the li (menuItem). So it is a descendant of the menu element (the ul#nav-menu). Yes, because the submenu is inside the li which is inside the ul. So the entire menu tree is under the nav-menu element. So checking relatedTarget against this.dom.menu will work: if relatedTarget is not a descendant of the menu element, then focus left the entire menu system.

Thus we can add:

this.dom.menu.addEventListener('focusout', (event) => {
  if (!this.dom.menu.contains(event.relatedTarget)) {
    // Focus left the menu
    if (this.elements.controller && this.elements.controller.isOpen) {
      this.elements.controller.close();
    }
  }
});

But we need to ensure we don't close when focus leaves due to something like scrolling? Should be fine.
